chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man bequeathed thirty dinars to the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her). He said: The man brought it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it to so-and-so, an elder from the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her), who was a provider and had dependents.' The man said to him: 'The man only bequeathed it to the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her).' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not fall to the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her) as a whole, but it falls to this man because he has dependents.'

6 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya wrote: 'Is it permissible for the executor to buy something from the deceased's property if it is sold, among those who increase [the price], and take it for himself?' He said: 'It is permissible if he buys a sound item.'

7 - From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ja'far ibn Isa, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a man who bequeathed part of his third after his death from the yield of his estate to his executor, to place it in specific places known to him every year, and the rest of the third, the executor should do with it as he wishes. The executor saw fit and executed what was bequeathed to him of the specified known [portion], and said regarding the rest: 'I have allocated so-and-so such-and-such every year, and for Hajj such-and-such, and for charity such-and-such every year.' Then it occurred to him regarding that, and he said: 'I desired the first, and I saw the opposite of my first desire and my opinion.' Is it for him to return in it, to allocate what he allocated to others, or to reduce them, or to include others with them if he wishes? He wrote to him (peace be upon him): 'He may do what he wishes, unless he wrote a document upon himself.'
ai.seo_question: Can an executor change the distribution of a bequest after executing it, and does a bequest to a group allow for selection of a specific member?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *maslaha* (public interest) in testamentary bequests, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prioritizes the welfare of dependents over strict literal adherence to a general beneficiary group. It further establishes the executor's discretionary authority (*tasarruf*) to manage remaining funds and the testator's right to modify allocations unless explicitly bound by a formal written covenant, reflecting the flexibility inherent in Shia inheritance law.
